supporting growing amounts of local energy generation. District energy and microgrid systems offer a promising path toward these goals, but their design andoperationarecomplex. Traditionally,thermalandelectricalnetworkshavebeenplanned and optimized separately, leading to inefficiencies, missed opportunities for coordinated op- eration, and slower adoption of emerging technologies. As energy sources such as solar photovoltaic(PV)systemsandwindgenerationbecomemoreprevalent,theneedforholistic evaluation tools continues to increase. These tools must support informed decision-making fromearlydesigntooperation. The grid-interactive efficient district (GED) initiative responds to this need by advancing an integrated approach to modeling, simulation, and optimization of coupled thermal-electric energy systems. Building on open-source tools and enabling multi-domain analysis, the project seeks to support communities, designers, and operators in creating more efficient, flexible,andresilientdistrictenergysystems. 1.2 ProjectOverview Coordinating the design of thermal, electrical and control networks is essential for the ad- vancement of GED energy systems, particularly as communities increasingly depend on re- newable energy resources and seek greater resilience through district energy networks and microgrids. Achieving these goals requires modeling tools that can represent the dynamic 1 interactions between energy domains while supporting rigorous design, analysis, and opti- mization. This project addresses this need by developing an open-source holistic modeling and opti- mization platform for the integrated design and retrofit of GED energy systems.
